description: We’re a diverse team of students passionate about space, technology, and problem-solving. Combining skills in coding, engineering, design, research, and communication, we aim to turn NASA’s data and challenges into creative, practical solutions. We’re excited to collaborate, experiment, and build something that makes a real impact
summary:
Earth Pulse Scan is an interactive climate trend detection platform designed to explore how Earth's environmental systems are changing over time. By integrating global and regional datasets from NASA, NOAA and other scientific institutions, Earth Pulse Scan analyses environmental indicators, including temperature, atmospheric CO₂, sea ice, sea levels, ocean heat content, vegetation and terrestrial water storage.

The platform scans dozens of regions worldwide, identifying opposing environmental trends and highlighting patterns across approximately 40 data points. By bringing together diverse scientific records, it helps users explore relationships between environmental indicators, recognise regional differences and understand how climate change affects different parts of the planet. It also incorporates future climate projections based on IPCC assessments, allowing users to investigate possible environmental changes under different scenarios.

Earth Pulse Scan addresses the Future Earth challenge by transforming complex scientific datasets into an accessible, interactive experience. By making environmental trends easier to discover and interpret, the platform promotes climate awareness, encourages curiosity and highlights the importance of scientific evidence in understanding Earth's changing systems and supporting informed decisions for a more sustainable future
details:
Earth Pulse Scan is an interactive climate investigation platform that makes global environmental data easier to explore and understand. Using a 3D globe, users can select locations worldwide and investigate environmental indicators such as temperature, rainfall, humidity, wind and solar irradiance through NASA POWER data.

The platform applies statistical techniques, including linear regression, Mann-Kendall and Theil-Sen analysis, to identify environmental trends and assess their significance. It also integrates scientific records from NASA, NOAA and other institutions, covering global temperatures, atmospheric CO₂, sea levels, sea ice, vegetation and terrestrial water storage.

Across ten interactive views, users can compare regional trends, explore historical climate records through a Time Machine, investigate relationships between environmental variables, examine counterfactual scenarios and explore future projections based on IPCC AR6 assessments. Guided missions and quizzes make the experience more engaging.

Built using React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Three.js and Recharts, the platform is hosted on Base44 and integrates the NASA POWER API with local caching. Gamma AI assisted with presentation development.

Our team prioritised scientific accuracy, accessibility and transparency. Missing data is never treated as zero, while sources and uncertainty are clearly presented. With no login required, Earth Pulse Scan aims to make climate science more accessible and encourage evidence-based environmental awareness.
